rationale: This is essentially the archive's "Debt-Issuance-Adjusted Fixed-Charge Profit" with the scaler switched from assets to the (dp+xint) denominator borrowed from "Liquid Fixed-Charge Coverage," a recombination of two already-tested constructs rather than a new mechanism, and the Δdebt subtraction mechanically rewards deleveraging firms (a known net-debt-issuance effect) rather than isolating coverage.

Since oibdp−dp ≈ oiadp, this is the already-evaluated "Liquidity-Backed Operating Strength" (MA(oiadp/at,3) bottlenecked by MA((act−lct)/at,3)) with only interest expense subtracted—a cosmetic variant of a signal that already delivered fmb 2.98 / alpha 3.6%.

Identical in structure to the archive's "Liquid Organizational Productivity" (oiadp/xsga × net-liquidity bottleneck) with only xint netted out of a numerator that is otherwise oiadp, so it is a marginal tweak rather than a substantively different hypothesis.

The construction is internally coherent and the sign direction is natural, but it differs from the archive's "Liability-Neutral Operating-Cost Cash Return" only by swapping the denominator from (cogs+xsga) to (dp+xint)—a scaler substitution with additional small-denominator instability—rather than testing a new economic channel, and it inherits that signal's already-thin ~6-7% coverage.

Both legs are lifted verbatim from prior evaluations (the stability-adjusted profitability leg from "Continuous Profit Reliability" and the debt-issuance-adjusted coverage leg from the first proposal in this batch), so while the pairing is new and economically sensible, it is a derivative leg-swap whose incremental information over the tested versions is likely small.

The two MIN legs share the identical numerator (oibdp−dp−xint) and differ only in scaler, so they are highly collinear and the "interaction" mainly reduces to sorting on after-charge earnings twice; the stated protection against small-denominator dominance is not achieved because the lct leg still mechanically favors firms with tiny current liabilities.
